newsitem.title: UK: L&G says 1996 new premium income up 54 pct.
newsitem.headline: L&G says 1996 new premium income up 54 pct.

text.p: British insurance Legal & General group said on Thursday that new UK equivalent premium income (EPI) rose 54 percent in 1996 to 301 million stg.
The company said all product areas showed significant growth with new life annual premiums rising 43 percent to 75.2 million stg.

"This impressive growth is the result of our strategy of providing consistently good value products through a range of distribution channels, backed by a strong investment team," said Legal & General chief executive David Prosser.
"We are selling more products to more customers, more efficiently and we continue to grow market share profitably."

In UK individual business, life single premiums rose 60 percent. Sales of PEPs and unit trusts reached 205.7 million stg, up from 177.4 million stg in 1995, reflecting the company's success in the index tracking market, it said.

In UK corporate, single premium new business of 724.6 million stg was more than four times the 1995 level of 175.8 million stg. UK pension fund assets continued to grow, with new funds under management nearly doubling to 4.25 billion stg.
New EPI from Legal & General's overseas life and pension business of 85.4 million stg reflected, in part, the strength of sterling and compared with 88.9 million stg in 1995.
